Introduction

Welcome to easy2edit, a simple, modular management system (CMS) for building and running portals, websites, webshops and communities. This manual explains how the system works and how to manage it from the admin screens.

## What is easy2edit

Easy2edit lets you build a website from blocks. Instead of writing code, you switch modules and plugins on or off, and arrange blocks on your pages to create the site you need. Under the hood, easy2edit runs on a Django (REST) backend with a Next.js frontend, but as an administrator you do not need to know the technical details to manage your site day to day.

Because the system is modular, you only use the parts you actually need. A simple website can run with just a handful of modules switched on, while a larger community or marketplace can use many more. Plugins extend this further by adding signed extension packages that bring their own pages and modules.

## Who uses easy2edit

There are three kinds of people who work with the system:

- Users: visitors who have created an account on the site. They use the front end of the site, such as viewing pages, taking part in a community or placing orders in a webshop.

- Admins: people who manage parts of the site. What an admin can see and do depends on the roles assigned to them. One admin might manage only pages and content, while another might manage users or orders, depending on their role.

- Superadmins: the owner or reseller of the installation. A superadmin has access to everything, including system settings, modules, plugins, pricing and the licence. This is the highest level of control in easy2edit.

## The dashboard

When you log in, you work from the dashboard. It is organised into three areas:

- Dashboard: your own profile, notifications and your own AI credit.

- Admin: the management area, where admins and superadmins manage the parts of the site they are responsible for.

- Super admin: the system area, available to superadmins only, for system-wide settings such as modules, plugins, pricing and the licence.

## Modules and plugins

Modules are parts of the system that can be switched on or off. You manage them at Super admin > Modules. Switching a module on makes its features available on the site; switching it off hides them again.

Plugins are signed extension packages that bring their own pages and modules. You manage plugins at Admin > Plugins. Installing and activating a plugin can add new modules and new pages to your site, extending what easy2edit can do beyond the core system.

Two modules are always part of every site and cannot be switched off: Energy & emissions and Energy: collector module. These are core modules and are on by default at every installation.

## Standard installations

To make it easy to start a new site, easy2edit offers standard installations. With one click, a standard installation sets the modules, plugins and theme for a particular type of website, such as a standard website, web shop, company website, business network, intranet, dating platform, sports club, foundation, marketplace or game hall.

There is also a test installation called "easy2edit max", which switches on everything: all modules and all plugins, with demo data everywhere. This is useful for exploring the full range of what easy2edit can do.

Each installation is shown as a small tile with a settings pop-up. This pop-up is visible in the admin area, and it is also offered the first time an installation is set up. It lets you configure AI credit settings, modules, plugins and demo data for that installation. The pop-up has five tabs: General, AI, Modules, Plugins and Demo data.

On the Plugins tab, a superadmin sees a switch for every plugin and every module belonging to the installation. Any change made here is saved immediately as the standard setup for the next time that type of installation is set up, and it is written to the installations file (backend/apps/core/installations.json) that other sites receive with an update. An administrator viewing the same tab sees the same list, but read-only, so they can see what is configured without being able to change it.

## The header

At the top of the screen, the header gives you quick access to:

- The language switcher, to change the display language.
- The edit-mode switch (pencil icon), to turn page editing on or off.
- Light and dark mode, to change the visual theme.
- The user menu, for your account options.

## Getting help

Help is always close at hand. On every page in the Admin and Super admin areas, a Help button (a question mark icon next to the back button) opens this manual in a pop-up, directly at the chapter relevant to the page you are viewing.

On the Admin start page, under About easy2edit, you will find two large buttons that give you the full manual: one opens the HTML version, either in a pop-up or in a new browser tab, and the other offers a PDF download. The manual is written in English.
Getting started

## Logging in for the first time

The very first time you open easy2edit, log in as superadmin. This account has full access to every setting and is the one you will use to set up the website.

If the site is running on your own computer (localhost), the system first asks whether you want to switch the sandbox on. With the sandbox on, payments, e-mail, sms and tests of API links are only simulated: nothing real is sent or charged, even if you have already entered live keys. Your answer is remembered, and you can change it later at Admin > Sandbox.

## Standard installation

If nothing has been installed yet, a pop-up appears offering a standard installation. It has two tabs:

- Installation: choose a ready-made setup to start from.
- Filling with AI: explains that the website can be filled with AI, for example by importing an existing website, translating content, or improving it with an instruction. This tab also shows whether an AI link is already available.

You can also start or change a standard installation later at Super admin overview or at Admin > Standard installations.

## Filling the site with AI

Once a standard installation has been set, the system asks whether you want to use AI to fill the site. If you choose yes, you go straight to buying AI credit. A welcome pop-up then explains what AI credit is and lets the superadmin set up the credit settings. See the AI chapter for details on how this works and how to manage it afterwards.

## Planting trees with easy2edit

During onboarding you may also see an optional step called "Plant trees with easy2edit":

- Choosing Yes switches the standard contributions on in test mode and links your website with the easy2edit server.
- Choosing No does nothing, and you can leave this for later.

If you continue, the price wizard asks whether you want to plant trees with easy2edit. There is a small monthly fee for management and overview, and the trees themselves cost about EUR 0.80 each, billed monthly by Ecologi. You can revisit and manage this later through the relevant Ecologi screens once the Ecologi connection is active.

## Setting up the basics

Once you have been through the initial pop-ups, work through the following settings to get your site ready:

1. Admin > System: enter the basic information about your site, such as the site name, company data, contact data and addresses.

2. Super admin overview or Admin > Standard installations: choose the standard installation that fits your website, if you have not done so already.

3. Admin > Theme: choose a theme for the look and feel of the site.

4. Admin > Logos / images: upload your logos and images.

5. Admin > Languages: choose which languages your website should offer.

6. Admin > Users and Roles: create the user accounts and roles you need, and decide who can do what.

## Finding your way around modules

easy2edit is built from modules, each covering one part of the system, such as pages, media, languages, users, payments or security. Modules can be switched on or off and configured individually. As you work through the steps above you will meet several of them directly, for example Admin > System, Admin > Theme, Admin > Languages and Admin > Users and Roles.

A full overview of all available modules, what they do and how to manage them, is provided in a later chapter. If you are a superadmin, you can always see the complete list of modules and their settings in the admin area.

## A good starting checklist

To summarise, a smooth first setup normally looks like this:

- Log in as superadmin.
- Decide on the sandbox setting if you are on localhost.
- Choose a standard installation, and decide whether to let AI help fill the site.
- Set up AI credit if you plan to use AI features.
- Decide whether to plant trees with easy2edit.
- Fill in your basic site information at Admin > System.
- Pick a theme and upload your logos and images.
- Choose your languages.
- Create the users and roles you need.

Once these steps are done, your website has its core identity, its content structure and its access rules in place, and you are ready to start building pages and adding content.
Pages, menu and edit mode

This chapter explains how pages are organised in easy2edit, how the menu works, and how to build and edit page content using edit mode and the page editor.

## Pages overview

Go to Admin > Pages to see all the pages on your site. There are several kinds of pages:

- System pages, such as Home or products, which belong to the system itself.
- Own pages: text pages that live at /p/<key>.
- Links and menu items, which point elsewhere or organise the menu.

For each page you can set:

- Names per language, with AI translation available to fill in all languages at once.
- The address per language.
- Who may see the page: everybody, logged-in users, guests, or specific users or groups.
- Whether it shows in the header menu.
- Whether it opens in a new tab.
- Which devices it appears on: desktop, tablet or mobile.
- A page-specific theme, header or footer.
- SEO settings per language.
- A background, which can be an image or a video.

## Switching on edit mode

To start editing a page, switch on the pencil icon in the header. This puts the page into edit mode, where you can add, move and change content directly on the page.

Pages are built from rows, also called blocks. Each row has cells, with one to four columns, and each cell holds items such as headings, text, images, buttons and more.

## Row and cell settings

Click the gear icon in the corner of a row to adjust:

- Background colour, image or video, with an optional overlay.
- Padding and width (column, wide, or full screen).
- Hero height.
- Text colour.
- Rounded corners.
- Space above the row.

Cell settings let you control width, alignment and card style, including background, border, radius and shadow.

Text items have their own settings: style, size, colour, font, padding and background (shown as a label or pill). Buttons can be set per language for their label, link, style (primary, outline or ghost), colours, size and icon.

## Items you can add

Within a cell you can add:

- Heading, text (rich text), image, button, spacer and line.
- System objects (see below).
- Ready-made parts: contact data, social media, map, video, quote, figures, logo and opening hours.
- The HTML / CSS code part.

## The HTML / CSS code part

This part opens in a large pop-up with three tabs: Visual, HTML and CSS. In the Visual tab you click directly into the text and type what you see is what you get, using a toolbar with bold, italic, underline, list, link and clear formatting. You can also switch between a light and dark background for editing. The code runs in a sandboxed frame and has no rights on the rest of the site.

## System objects

System objects include donation buttons, subscriptions, media views, plugin parts and, for superadmins, AI dashboard blocks. The relevant module must be switched on in Admin > System objects. In edit mode, add them through + Add > System objects.

## Pages imported from HTML

If a page was taken over 1 to 1 from an HTML file during site import, every text and button shows a pencil in edit mode. Click the pencil to open an editor that displays the text as it appears on the page, with bold, italic, underline and link options, plus the button's link if applicable. Click Save to write your changes back into the page.

## The page editor

The page editor works like a page builder, with a bar on top and a panel on the left, next to the page itself.

The top bar has:

- Elements, Structure, Page and Settings tabs.
- The name of the page.
- A Saved indicator, since every change is saved at once.
- The Done button.

The left panel can be collapsed to a narrow strip, which stays visible so you can reopen it, and can be dragged wider or narrower.

### Elements tab

Elements are grouped into Basic (heading, text, image, button, quote), Media (logo, map, video, and the Media library as an unfolding button), About the company, Layout, Components (searchable, from your component set) and System (system objects grouped per module or plugin).

Click an element to add it at the bottom of the chosen column, or drag it onto the page. You can drop it into a column, before or after another part, or onto the line between two blocks to start a new block. While dragging, the lines between blocks and columns highlight to show where the element will land.

### Structure tab

Shows the list of blocks and columns, with Up and Down controls to reorder them.

### Page tab

Shows the settings for the whole page: names per language, address, SEO, background, width and items per page.

### Settings tab

Shows the settings for whatever you have selected on the page: a text or heading (style, size, colour, font, space), an image (alignment, size, opacity, rounded corners, zoom, shadow and mouse-over effect), a button, a part, the header or the footer.

## Editing parts directly on the page

When you hover over a part, a pencil and a cross appear at its top right corner, in that order. The pencil opens it for editing in the panel, the cross deletes it.

- A column has its own pencil and cross at its top right corner. The cross empties the column; an empty column then disappears.
- A block or hero has its pencil and cross in its top right corner.
- Between two blocks is a thin line with three controls: + to add a new block (choose the structure, including hero options), a pencil to edit the block above, and a cross to delete it.

## Display and other tools

At the foot of the panel, Display lets you preview the page as it would look on computer, iPad or phone. The page next to the panel updates to that width and refreshes after every change.

The question mark at the top right switches on Help: point at any control to read what it does.

In every colour picker you can save your own colours with +, up to 16 per user, available on every computer you use. Change a saved colour with the pencil or remove it with the cross. Sliders and tabs follow your theme.

## Menu settings

Go to Admin > Pages > Menu to configure the header menu:

- Menu items can be shown in lower case or capitals.
- Set the font size.
- Decide when the menu becomes a hamburger menu: when it does not fit, below a certain width, when there are more than a set number of items, or always.

A live example shows your settings as you adjust them.

## Using the AI button in the page editor

The AI button in the top bar of the page editor improves the page as a whole, adjusting space, alignment, sizes, colours and hero height.

Changes are shown as css and html differences, with old code in red and new code in green, alongside a progress bar and a live counter of the AI cost.

The AI panel has these tabs:

- Instruction, where you describe what you want.
- Page, showing the current page.
- Photos and videos, with suggestions and search terms.
- Stock, offering free Pexels and Unsplash photos and Pexels videos; click Use to place one into the page.

Every AI action counts as a single undo step. Undo it with the arrow at the top right or with Ctrl/Cmd+Z.

To use the AI button, Claude must be linked to your site. The Stock tab additionally needs Pexels or Unsplash linked.
Importing a website (Site import)

Site import lets you turn an existing website, a set of HTML files or a prompt built with an external AI into a ready-made easy2edit site. Nothing is created on your website until you have seen the proposal and approved it.

You find this feature under Admin > Imported. The button is called 'Site import' until you have imported a site for the first time; after that it is called 'Imported'.

## Starting an import

You can start from an HTML file, several HTML files, a web address, a folder or a ZIP file. Drop or point to the source and the AI reads it. It then makes a proposal containing:

- a theme (colours, fonts, corner roundings, content width)
- pages and their content
- icons and images, which are placed in the media library with the tag 'import'
- the modules that are needed, for example the FAQ module for a list of questions

Review the proposal. Nothing is built on your site until you approve it.

## Designing a website with AI (Website design)

Under Admin > Imported, tab AI creator, the button New design opens a wizard with seven steps: Start, Style, Colours, Pages, Modules, Photos, Preview. The design is saved automatically while you work. If you close the window while the design is still a concept, you are asked whether to save it under My designs, delete it, or go back and continue.

## Quick start with an external AI

The first step of the wizard has a block called 'Quick start with an external AI'. It explains three steps:

1. Choose which modules and plugins the site needs.
2. Copy the prompt and paste it into an external AI such as Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini.
3. Read the resulting ZIP file back into easy2edit.

The button 'Copy AI prompt' builds the full prompt from all your choices and copies it to the clipboard. The button 'Modules and plugins (n/m)' lets you switch each module and plugin on or off. Modules and plugins that are part of your active standard installation are switched on by default. Switching on something extra shows a warning that your monthly price will go up, and by how much (ex VAT); the new total monthly price is shown under the list. Only what is switched on is used in the prompt, by the AI, and later by the import.

The prompt itself includes the design guidelines of the page editor (bands, hero, cells, cards, blocks), the rules for building the ZIP file, and, for every extra language of the website, the format of a translation file.

## The ZIP file

The ZIP you read back in (tab ZIP file, or 'Read ZIP file' in the design wizard) must follow these rules:

- at most 12 HTML pages, each HTML file becomes one page, including pages only linked from the footer
- one style.css
- a folder img/ with at most 40 pictures (jpg, png, webp or svg), each at most 5 MB, with file names in lowercase letters, digits, - and _, at most 40 characters long
- everything must sit in the top folder of the ZIP; other folders are skipped, and a note tells you so

Backgrounds referenced from the CSS, including through CSS variables, are taken along, and SVG files are cleaned. A file name that breaks the rules is renamed automatically, and every reference to it in the HTML and CSS is rewritten to match.

For every extra language, the ZIP can include a file vertalingen-<code>.json, in the format easy2edit-vertalingen/1. It states the source language, the target language, and per page a list of items with the element, the source text and the translation. When the site is translated, these texts are used first; only what is missing is translated by the AI. The import notes report what was skipped, and how many texts came from the file versus from the AI.

## Applying the import

Once you approve the proposal, the theme is installed and put to use. Then the Apply panel opens, with tabs Pages, Links, Buttons, Header, Footer and Theme.

Pages: drag pages from the file (left column) onto pages of your website (right column), for example onto Home, or leave a file page as its own new page. Choose the view:

- Exact: the page looks exactly like the HTML file; texts and buttons can still be edited with the pencil in edit mode
- Editable: the AI rebuilds the page using the blocks of the page builder (cards, label pills, band colours, rows, hero); anything the blocks cannot reproduce, such as a progress bar, check list or preview cards, becomes an 'HTML / CSS code' block

You can give the AI an optional instruction, for example "make the headings bigger". Choose what happens to content already on the page: clear it first, replace only the blocks from this import, or add the new content below. You can also choose whether the pages should be translated into the other languages of the site.

Links and Buttons: drag and drop to connect the links and buttons from the file to pages or parts of your website.

Header: switch the system header to the header from the file, giving a bigger menu with the file's links and buttons.

Footer: show the system footer under the imported pages.

Theme: adjust colours, default mode, content width and corner roundings.

Progress is shown in a pop-up with a percentage; when the import is ready, a 'Go to page' button appears. The original HTML is always kept, so you can apply the import again later with a new instruction. Each import has a status, Pending or Active, and its page list shows, per page: name, whether it is in the menu, whether it is visible, and which view is used.

In Admin > Pages, under page settings, an imported page has an extra tab called Import, where you can give the AI a new instruction and rebuild just that one page from the original file.

## Removing an import

Removing an import restores the theme and content that were on the pages before, or, if that is not possible, advises you to reinstall via the superadmin; it also removes everything the import created. The standard home page (logo, title, text, photos) is always left empty and is overwritten by an import, so it never shows through behind an imported homepage.

## Building an AI prompt from scratch

Admin > Imported, tab AI creator, button Make AI prompt opens an 11-step wizard that helps you describe what a good website needs:

1. the company
2. goal and visitors
3. pages and content
4. contact details
5. style
6. theme, colours and components
7. imagery
8. functions (modules)
9. language and findability
10. inspiration and extra wishes
11. design files

At step 6 you choose a theme and a component set; the colours of the theme automatically fill the colour fields. Every answer you give is added to the prompt as 'the brief'. The button 'To the prompt' on each step sends your answers straight to the prompt tab.

If you do not provide design files, the AI designs the entire website from the brief and delivers an import ZIP.

A chosen theme adds its CSS variables for light and dark mode, its fonts and its corner roundings to the prompt as mandatory conditions. A chosen component set adds the list of its components, each with its easy2edit_tag and the set key. During import, easy2edit recognises data-easy2edit-tag and data-easy2edit-set attributes in the HTML, turns each into a matching component block, and draws it using your theme while ignoring the component's own CSS. The import report lists which components were recognised, which set the design used, and which tags were unknown.
Media, theme, languages and branding

## Media library

The media library is where you manage all images and videos for your website, whether they are stored locally or on Amazon S3. You can add tags to your files to keep them organised and easy to find.

Once a file is in the media library, it becomes available everywhere in the system. Whenever you open a pop-up to choose a picture, for example when editing a page, a component or your branding settings, you can pick directly from the library instead of uploading the same file again.

## Logos and images (branding)

Go to Admin > Website > Logos & images to manage the visual identity of your site:

- Logo for light mode and logo for dark mode
- Favicon
- App icon
- The photos shown on the home page

Because light and dark versions of the logo are managed separately, your branding stays consistent no matter which mode a visitor is using.

## Theme (Admin > Theme)

The theme controls the overall look and feel of your website. When the theme is switched off, the website uses the standard style. When it is switched on, you can configure:

- Colours for light mode and dark mode
- Fonts
- Roundings (how sharp or soft corners appear)
- Content width
- Header layout, including the editorial layout with a side menu
- Pop-up style
- Theme packs, which you can switch with a single click
- Export and import of themes, useful for reusing a look on another site or keeping a backup

Because components are built directly into the page and follow the active theme, changing the theme updates the colours, fonts and corners of every component automatically. There is no need to redesign each component separately.

## Components (Admin > Components)

Components are ready-made building blocks for your pages, such as navigation bars, content blocks, data tables, charts and footers. They automatically pick up the colours, fonts and corner styles of your active theme, and they can also be reached as a tab inside Admin > Theme.

Every component has its own easy2edit_tag. This tag is used when you export or import components, when you design them, and when you write AI prompts that reference a specific component.

The standard set, easy2edit UI-kit, contains 100 components organised in groups:

- Start
- Basic
- Navigation
- Content blocks
- Database and lists (including a data table with search and sorting, a table with selection and bulk actions, a list of records, a grid of cards with search and filters, a search page, a filter bar, record detail, record form, and list with detail)
- Web shop
- Data and feedback
- Charts and statistics (including bar, horizontal bar, stacked bar, line, area, multiple lines, pie, gauge, rings, trend figures, heat map, funnel, progress bars, target bar, leaderboard, radar, comparison, and chart with period choice)
- Planning and agenda (calendars, schedule, year view, kanban, planning)
- Business
- Media
- Footer

The tabs you see for components follow the settings in Theme > Appearance > Tabs.

## More component sets

Besides the UI-kit, easy2edit offers alternative sets with the same 100 components in a different style: Zacht (soft), Strak (sharp), Speels (playful) and Glas (glass).

Each set is delivered as a zip file containing components.json, components.css and components.js, stored in resource/components. In the Sets tab you can see which sets are installed on your website, browse the library of available sets, install or remove a set, choose the active one, or upload your own zip file.

To use a component on a page, open the page editor and go to Elements > Components. If you want to reference components in an AI prompt, the List tab provides a ready-made list with the easy2edit_tag of every component, which you can copy straight into your prompt.

## Web templates (Admin > Website > Templates)

A web template is a complete starting website delivered as a single zip file in resource/templates, including pages, pictures, menu structure and example images, and sometimes a theme or component set as well.

To use a template:

1. Go to Admin > Website > Templates and browse the available templates.
2. Preview the example pictures to see what the template looks like.
3. Choose to add the template next to your existing pages, or replace pages that share the same address.

Once applied, everything from the template is fully yours to edit in the page editor.

Templates are added or removed by a superadmin, either through the Templates tab in Super admin > Library or directly on the Templates page.

## Languages

Go to Admin > Website > Languages to manage multilingual support. When languages are switched off, the website shows only the default language.

When switched on, you can:

- Choose which languages your website offers
- Set the default language
- Translate texts using the built-in AI translation

The system interface itself is already available in 44 languages.

## Loading animation

The standard loader in easy2edit is a green tree inside a circle, configured at Admin > Website > Theme > Loading, under the kind "Green tree (standard)". Loading is always shown as an animation, never as text.
Users, roles and security

Easy2edit gives you fine control over who can access your site, what they are allowed to do once they are in, and how the site protects itself and its visitors. This chapter explains users, user groups, roles and the security tools available in the admin area.

## Users

Every person who needs access to the admin area or a personal presence on the website has an account under Users. From here you can:

- Create new accounts
- Block accounts temporarily
- Delete accounts that are no longer needed

Each user account can have a profile photo and an openbaar profile, which can be shown on the website. This is useful for authors, moderators or team members who should be visible to visitors.

## User groups

If you manage many accounts, it is often easier to work with user groups rather than individual users. A user group is a collection of users that share the same roles and the same module access. Instead of configuring rights for each person separately, you assign rights once to the group, and every member automatically receives them.

This is particularly helpful for teams such as editors, moderators or support staff, where everyone in the team needs the same level of access.

## Roles and rights

Roles (Rollen) define what a user or group is allowed to do inside the admin area. A role is simply a named set of rights, for example:

- Content manager
- Moderator
- View AI use of users

Each right unlocks a specific part of the admin area. By combining rights into roles, you can tailor access precisely to what a team member needs, without giving them full administrative control.

Superadmins always have every right, regardless of the roles configured. If the Rollen module itself is switched off, only superadmins have any rights at all, so make sure this module stays enabled once you start delegating work to other staff.

## Module access per user or group

In addition to roles, individual modules can be switched on or off for a specific user or group. This is managed under Super admin > Modules, using the person icon. This gives you an extra layer of control: even if someone has a role with broad rights, you can still decide exactly which modules they are allowed to use.

## Dashboard and profile

Once logged in, every user lands on their dashboard, where they can manage their own profile. This is also where the login process itself takes place. Encourage users to keep their profile information and photo up to date, especially if their profile is shown publicly on the site.

## General security settings

Under Algemene beveiliging you configure the baseline security behaviour for the whole site:

- Inlogslot (login lock) to stop repeated failed login attempts
- Sessieduur (session time) to control how long a user stays logged in
- Wachtwoordregels (password rules) to enforce stronger passwords
- Beveiligingsheaders (security headers) to strengthen the technical protection of the site

Review these settings early on, since they form the foundation of your site's overall security posture.

## Two-step verification

Two-step verification adds a second check in addition to the password when logging in. By default, it is required for all admins and superadmins, ensuring that the most powerful accounts are the best protected.

If someone is blocked because of a problem with two-step verification, an email is automatically sent to the administrator, so access issues can be resolved quickly.

## Country control

The Landcontrole module lets you block or allow access to the website based on the visitor's country, using IP-based checks. This is useful if your content or services should only be available in certain regions.

## Age check and gambling warning

Two modules help you meet age-related legal requirements:

- Leeftijdscontrole shows an 18+ popup to visitors before they can view the site.
- Gokken-popup shows a combined age and warning popup specifically for gambling-related content.

Enable whichever of these applies to your website's content.

## Cookies

The Cookies module manages the cookie banner shown to visitors, their saved preferences, and a cookie policy popup. This helps you present cookie information clearly and keep a record of visitor consent.

## Word filter

The Woordfilter module lets you define a list of forbidden words. These words are then automatically checked for in texts, names and captions submitted on the site, helping you keep user-generated content appropriate.

## Practical tips

- Start by setting up roles and user groups before creating many individual accounts, so new users can be added quickly with the right access.
- Keep two-step verification enabled for all admin and superadmin accounts.
- Review login lock, session time and password rules together, since they work hand in hand to protect accounts.
- Turn on age checks, gambling warnings or country control only if they are relevant to your content, to avoid unnecessary friction for visitors.
Shop, orders, payments, subscriptions and donations

Easy2edit offers a set of connected plugins that together turn your website into a fully working shop, membership system or donation platform. Depending on what you want to achieve, you combine the Webshop, Orders, Financieel and Abonnementen plugins. This chapter explains what each plugin does and how they work together.

## How the plugins relate to each other

These four plugins are designed to work as a system rather than as separate tools.

- Webshop needs Orders and Betalen (Payments) to function, since it relies on them for handling orders and processing payments.
- Orders manages orders for the whole site: webshop orders, subscriptions and donations. It can also work on its own, for example if you only want to accept payment by invoice.
- Financieel brings everything related to money together: payment methods, VAT rates, shipping options and document layout. Orders, Webshop and Abonnementen all depend on this plugin.
- Abonnementen (Subscriptions) needs Orders, since every subscription period or donation generates an order.

In short, Orders and Financieel form the backbone, while Webshop and Abonnementen build on top of them depending on whether you are selling products or offering access and donations.

## Setting up the webshop

The Webshop plugin lets you build a complete online store, including:

- Products and product groups
- Variants such as colour and size, each with their own price
- Staggered pricing (staffelprijzen), where the price changes depending on quantity
- Shipping methods
- Discount codes
- Several layout options: a standard layout, an editorial layout with a filter side panel and large product photos, and a "shop the look" layout
- Styles and presets to match the look of your shop to your website

The plugin comes with demo content, including ready-made shop pages for products, the shopping cart and checkout, so you can see a working example before customising it.

To get a webshop running:

1. Make sure the Orders and Betalen (Payments) plugins are installed and activated.
2. Set up your products and product groups, including any variants and pricing.
3. Configure shipping methods and, if needed, discount codes.
4. Review the demo shop pages and adjust the layout, styles and presets to fit your site.

## Managing orders

The Orders plugin is the central place for order management across your whole site. It handles orders coming from the webshop, from subscriptions and from donations, all in one overview.

With Orders you can manage:

- Order status, so you always know what stage each order is in
- VAT settings applied to orders
- The confirmation email sent to customers
- Documents linked to each order, such as the packing slip, invoice, return slip and credit invoice

Orders does not require a full webshop to work. It can be used on its own if you simply want to accept orders and let customers pay by invoice, without setting up products or online payment.

## Financieel: payments, VAT and documents

The Financieel plugin is where everything related to money comes together. It is required by Orders, Webshop and Abonnementen, so most setups will need it configured correctly.

In Financieel you manage:

- Payment methods and payment terms
- The connections to Stripe and Mollie for processing online payments
- VAT rates, with a standard high and low rate that you link to individual products
- Shipping options
- The layout of your financial documents: invoices, quotes, packing slips and return slips
- Your company details used on these documents

Payments themselves run through Stripe or Mollie. Before going live, you can use the sandbox to simulate payments, allowing you to test the full payment flow without processing real transactions.

To set up payments:

1. Go to the Financieel plugin and connect your Stripe or Mollie account.
2. Set your VAT rates and link them to the relevant products.
3. Configure shipping options and payment terms.
4. Adjust the layout of invoices, quotes, packing slips and return slips to match your branding.
5. Test the setup using the sandbox before accepting real payments.

## Subscriptions and donations

The Abonnementen plugin lets you offer paid or free access to parts of your site, as well as collect donations. It requires the Orders plugin, since each billing period creates an order.

Subscriptions can:

- Give access to pages, content, chat, video, likes or services
- Be set up as a one-off purchase or as a repeated subscription
- Generate a new order automatically for each period, for repeated subscriptions

Subscriptions are organised through plans and actions. A plan defines what a subscriber gets access to, while actions determine what is free and what requires payment.

Donations work in a similar way but are structured as gifts. Visitors choose an amount using a slider, which you configure with a minimum and maximum value, rather than selecting a fixed plan.

To set up subscriptions or donations:

1. Make sure the Orders plugin is active.
2. Create a plan describing what access or benefit it provides.
3. Choose whether the plan is a one-off purchase or a repeating subscription.
4. For donations, set up a donation action and configure the slider with your desired minimum and maximum amount.
5. Define which actions make content or access free, and which require payment.
Community, marketplace, agenda, documents and games

This chapter covers the plugins that turn your site into a place where members connect, trade, plan, share files and play. Together they can power a full community or dating site, a marketplace, a shared calendar, a document library and a small games arcade.

## Community overview

The Community plugin bundles everything you need for a community or dating site: profile pages with photos, a member search, blocking, discovery (liking, matching, favourites, visitors), private messages, chat, and a direct WebRTC connection using a code, link or QR code. It also supports profile themes, profile fields and "available for" options.

When parts of the community require a subscription or donation, Community works together with the Subscriptions plugin to handle access.

## Profile themes

Profile themes define which fields and filters appear on member profiles. Ready-made packages are included for Sporters, Dating, Business and Webshop, and you can install or remove them as needed. You can also build your own theme with custom fields, visibility settings and search filters.

The superadmin decides which themes are available for admins and users to choose. Themes can be exported and imported as JSON, which makes it easy to reuse a theme on another site.

## Profiles and blocking

Each member gets a profile page with multiple photos. Visibility can be set per language and per group, so you control who sees what. The member search helps users find each other, and members can block other users they do not want contact with.

## Discover: searching and matching

The discover feature works like a dating site: members can search with filters, see recommendations, like other profiles, get matches, save favourites and see who has visited their profile.

## Messages and chat

- Messages: a private messaging system between members, with its own inbox.
- Chat: chat in a popup or full screen, either through the portal or directly between members using WebRTC, including photos, video and video chat.

## Direct connection

Direct connect sets up a direct WebRTC connection between two people using a code, link or QR code, without needing an account. It supports chat, photos, video and video chat, and is available on the pages /directconnect and /direct.

## Marketplace

In the marketplace, members can offer products, services or anything else for sale, with a theme and images. Three sale types are supported:

- A fixed price.
- Bidding, starting from a minimum price, with bids visible to all members.
- A booking, for example an appointment or a sign-up for an event.

## Agenda

The agenda gives users and groups their own calendar. It supports:

- Personal appointments.
- Appointments with other members, including invitations, confirmations or proposing another time.
- Group appointments.
- Events created by administrators, which can be placed on pages as a system object.

Reminders and notifications keep members informed, and a tile on the dashboard gives a quick overview of upcoming items.

## Document management

Documents can be uploaded into a folder structure, with tags, versions and access rights set per user or per group. Files are stored on the server or on S3, and can be encrypted. Blocks are available to show documents directly on pages.

## Games

The games section gives members a small games arcade. Each game is its own package, a folder or zip containing a game.json file, placed in the games folder of the plugin. Every game has its own configuration for administrators and its own settings per member. Games run in a sandboxed, isolated way and save scores and progress. Ranking lists and a sample game are included to help you get started.

## Age, country and gambling checks

Age verification (18+), country checks and the gambling popup (24+) are available for target groups where this is required or desired. The settings for these checks live under Admin > Security, but the popups and country check only work when this community-related plugin is switched on.

## Showcase

Showcase lets you present projects such as campaigns, portfolio items or initiatives. Each project can include a title, short text, description, goal, link, duration, budget, pictures and videos (YouTube, Vimeo or an mp4/webm link), a status (active, in development, offline), tags and groups. Every field can be switched on or off in the plugin settings, shown as switches in columns.

Tags are shared across projects, so the same tag can label many projects. Groups can have subgroups, and selecting a group automatically includes its subgroups.

The admin page, Admin > Plugins > Showcase, has four tabs: Projects, Groups, Tags and Presentations. A project is edited in a popup with the tabs General, Content, Media and Translations.

Presentations control how a selection of projects is displayed:

- Layouts: grid, list, table, photo wall (masonry), scroller or slider.
- Opening behaviour: its own page (/showcase/<name>), a popup, or in place.
- Optional search field and filters on tags, groups and status.
- Option to show only certain fields, a specific group, specific tags, a specific status, or only featured projects.

Every active presentation is a system object you can place on a page in edit mode. Three standard presentations (search, scroller, list) always exist. Public pages are available at /showcase and /showcase/<name>.

Demo content, consisting of 9 sample projects, groups, tags and 6 presentations, can be created or removed with a single button on the plugin page, making it easy to explore Showcase before adding your own projects.
SEO, FAQ and statistics

## Overview

This chapter covers three related tools that help you understand and improve how your website performs: SEO settings, the FAQ module, and the statistics dashboard. Together they help search engines, bots and AI agents find and understand your content, let you answer common visitor questions directly on your site, and give you insight into how your site is actually being used.

## SEO

The SEO tools help search engines, bots and AI agents read and understand your website correctly. This includes:

- robots.txt, which tells search engines and bots which parts of your site they may or may not visit
- A sitemap, which lists all your pages so search engines can find them more easily
- llms.txt, a file aimed specifically at AI agents and language models, helping them understand your site structure and content
- Page titles and descriptions, shown in search results and often used by AI agents when summarizing or referencing your site
- Structured data, which adds machine-readable information to your pages so search engines and AI tools can better interpret what a page is about

Because these settings affect how both traditional search engines and newer AI-based tools interact with your site, it is worth reviewing them whenever you add important new pages or change your site structure significantly.

## FAQ

The FAQ module lets you build your own list of frequently asked questions and answers, shown on the page /faq.

Key points about the FAQ module:

- You create and manage the questions and answers yourself.
- Questions and answers can be translated into all languages your site supports.
- If you imported an existing site, any questions found during the import are automatically placed into this module, so you do not lose existing FAQ content.

To make the FAQ page accessible to visitors through your site navigation:

1. Go to Admin > Pages.
2. Add the /faq page to your menu, just as you would any other page.

Once added, visitors can navigate to your FAQ page like any other part of the site, and you can keep the list of questions up to date as new topics come up.

## Statistics

The statistics section gives you a clear picture of what is happening across your entire website, combining visitor numbers, SEO performance, bot activity and AI calls into one place, with charts and figures.

What you can see here includes:

- Overall visitor statistics for your website
- SEO-related figures, showing how your site is being found and indexed
- Bot activity, tracking automated visits from search engines and other crawlers
- AI calls, showing activity from AI agents accessing your site
- A separate tab for each module and plugin that reports its own statistics

Each module and plugin that supports statistics writes its own numbers into this section, shown as its own tab with relevant widgets and charts. This means the statistics dashboard grows naturally as you enable more modules and plugins, each contributing its own relevant data.

An important detail to keep in mind: if a particular plugin is switched off, nothing is counted for it. Statistics are only gathered while a module or plugin is active, so turning something off will pause its data collection until it is switched on again.

## Practical tips

- Review your SEO settings, including page titles, descriptions and structured data, whenever you publish new important pages, since this directly affects how both search engines and AI agents represent your site.
- Keep your FAQ page linked in your main menu so visitors can easily find answers without needing to contact you directly.
- If you imported an existing site, check the FAQ module afterwards to confirm that any imported questions were captured correctly and translated where needed.
- Check the statistics dashboard regularly, not just the overall visitor numbers but also the per-module and per-plugin tabs, to see which parts of your site are actively being used or crawled.
- If you notice a module or plugin is not showing any statistics, confirm that it is actually switched on, since inactive plugins do not record any data.
AI and AI credit

Easy2edit uses artificial intelligence, powered by Claude (Anthropic), throughout the system. It helps with translating content, writing page texts, importing websites, researching prices and more. Because AI calls have a real cost, every call is logged and, in most cases, paid for with AI credit.

## How AI is switched on

AI is a core module. It becomes active automatically as soon as an AI link (an API key) is installed and enabled under Admin > API keys.

A link can be marked as a Superadmin link. In that case only superadmins can see or change it. This is used, for example, for the easy2edit AI link and the Stripe link of the reseller, which must stay out of reach of regular admins.

When a superadmin has an easy2edit AI link installed, all AI calls made by users and admins run on that link. This keeps billing and monitoring centralised unless an admin has set up their own AI link, as described further below.

## Monitoring every call

Every single call to the AI is recorded, including:

- Who made the call: a user, an admin, a superadmin, or the system itself
- From which part of the system the call came
- Which AI model was used
- Tokens sent in and tokens received out
- How long the call took
- Whether it succeeded
- What it cost

This information feeds the Super admin > AI dashboard.

## The Super admin AI dashboard

Superadmins manage AI through Super admin > AI, which has these tabs:

- Overview: key figures, cost over time per group, share of use per group, and the last calls made
- Where: where AI is used most, what costs most, which tasks and models are involved, and the busiest hours and weekdays
- Users: heavy users, highest costs, and a table per user with a PDF button on each row
- Costs: costs broken down per month or week, per group, and per user
- Credit: management of AI credit balances
- Blocks: dashboard blocks that can be placed on pages
- Settings: pricing and margin configuration

The dashboard can be filtered by period, by month (the current month plus the twelve before it), and by group. The PDF button produces a summary; choosing 'Detailed' produces a complete list of every call with tokens in and out, duration and costs.

## Costs, pricing and margins

Superadmins configure purchase prices per million tokens per model under the Claude, OpenAI and Gemini tabs, matching whichever models are active in the connected API. The 'Refresh models' button looks up current prices directly from the AI provider.

Purchase prices are set in the purchase currency (for example USD), while sale prices are set in the selling currency (for example EUR), using an exchange rate that can be updated with a button that asks the AI for the current rate.

Three separate margins can be set, each split between tokens in and tokens out:

- Users
- Admins
- Reseller/superadmin

A switch decides whether superadmin and system use is also charged to the customer. When switched on, this use is booked to a group named after the website, with the reseller margin applied. When switched off, this use is a cost to the reseller with no margin, shown separately.

Prices, exchange rate and margins are stored with each individual call, so any later change to settings only affects new calls, never past ones. Only superadmins can change these AI settings.

## AI credit

By default, users and admins must buy AI credit before they can use AI features. Superadmins and the system itself never need credit.

Before every AI call, the system estimates its cost and checks it against the available credit. If there is not enough credit, nothing is sent, and a message explains how much is needed.

After the call completes, the actual cost is deducted from the credit balance.

When a user's credit is low, a pop-up appears with a slider to top up, offering a minimum of 25, 50 or 100 based on the user's usage over the last 30 days, along with a suggested amount.

Payment always runs through Stripe using an easy2edit link belonging to the superadmin, never the website's own shop Stripe. Credit is added once payment is confirmed, which happens when the customer returns from Stripe and again when the AI screen is opened.

Superadmins set the top-up amounts and can manually add or deduct credit per user via Super admin > AI > Credit.

Every admin sees a welcome pop-up at first login explaining how AI and AI credit work.

On any computer where the sandbox is switched on, AI credit is never paid with a real payment. Instead, the simulated payment page is used.

Each standard installation has an AI tab showing whether AI belongs to that installation, whether credit is required, and the smallest and biggest allowed top-up amounts.

## What admins can see

Admin > AI shows the AI use of users and admins, without purchase prices or margin details or any reseller costs. It includes a block called 'AI use' on the Admin start page, showing the admin's own credit, a table per user and a PDF report per user that excludes purchase prices.

To see this, an admin needs the right 'View AI use of users', assigned under Roles.

## Admins with their own AI link

An admin who has set up their own Anthropic AI link and their own Stripe link, with neither marked as a superadmin link, can switch on their own credit system for their users via Admin > AI > Credit for users.

In that case:

- Their users use the admin's own AI link
- Payments run through the admin's own Stripe account
- The margin belongs to the admin
- The admin sets the credit rules, top-up amounts and margin
- The admin can add credit per user manually

## AI blocks on pages

Parts of the AI dashboard, such as key figures, cost over time, use per group, where AI is used, heavy users, highest costs, models and busy hours, can be switched on as system objects under Super admin > AI > Blocks and placed on any page in edit mode. Only superadmins can see the figures in these blocks.
Plugins, backups, licence and deployment

This chapter explains how to manage plugins, protect your site with backups, understand your licence and pricing, and deploy and maintain easy2edit, including the system's built-in tree-planting features.

## Plugins

Plugins are managed from Admin > Plugins. They are signed packages stored in /plugins and can be installed from the library (resource/plugins), switched on or off, and updated.

A plugin can bring its own pages, modules, translations (44 languages) and admin screens. If a plugin has demo content, its page in Admin > Plugins (tab Overview) shows a button:

- 'Make demo content' when no demo content exists yet.
- 'Remove demo content' once it has been created, letting you take it away again.

Resetting the system also removes any demo content.

The module API keys is always on in every standard installation. The superadmin links (AI, Stripe, mail, storage) are switched on automatically when an installation is set up, so they keep working, but the secret keys themselves are never stored in the installations file. A link marked Superadmin link is only visible and editable by superadmins.

Resetting the system (Super admin > System > Reset) asks whether AI data in the database should be removed too, meaning all AI calls with costs plus the credit history and credit of superadmins (the AI settings themselves stay). The credit of normal users disappears automatically when those users are removed.

## Importing a site

Admin lets you import another website from an address, folder, ZIP file or a single HTML file, bringing in its theme, pages, home page, icons and images. When importing a single HTML file, Claude builds the theme, pages and content, and switches on the modules that are needed. An imported site can be removed again, together with everything that came with it.

## Backups

Backups are available in Admin > Backups, with daily, weekly and monthly backups covering pages, menus, texts, images, the theme and the settings of modules and plugins.

Practical steps:

1. In the backup list, click Download to download a backup at once; progress is shown with a progress bar.
2. Click Make backup now to create a fresh backup. You will then be asked whether to download it, keep it locally, or both.
3. After uploading a backup file, easy2edit immediately asks whether you want to restore it.

A restore brings back the logo, base data, theme and licence data exactly, and shows them right away. Back office loaders stay small during these actions; the large loader appears as its own layer in the middle of the window only for bigger operations.

The standard installations basis (installations.json) is part of the system itself. As with plugins and API keys, secret keys are never stored in this file.

## Licence and pricing

Admin > Licence shows the cost and payment method of your licence, either Stripe or invoice. The price follows directly from the modules and plugins that are switched on.

Super admin > Prices holds the full price list per month, quarter and year, together with quotations as PDF, marketing tiles and the sales calculation used to work out pricing.

## Deployment

easy2edit is deployed with Docker, using separate compose files for development and production. A reverse proxy and certificates handle secure access, and the backend runs database migrations automatically on start.

Every installation shows its version in the format 'easy2edit version 1.0.0 build X', sourced from one central place: backend/BUILD.

## SEO and site visibility

easy2edit helps search engines, bots and AI agents understand your site through robots.txt, a sitemap, llms.txt, page titles, descriptions and structured data.

## Statistics

Admin statistics show graphs and figures for the whole website: visitors, SEO, bots and AI calls, plus a separate tab per module and plugin. Modules and plugins write their own figures here; if a plugin is switched off, nothing is counted for it.

## Trees and gifts

easy2edit can plant trees through Ecologi, reflecting the site's own energy and growth.

At superadmin level, the module 'ecologi' adds a Super admin menu item 'easy2edit' with a page containing the tabs Overview, Plant trees, Contributions, Costs, History and Settings, plus a block 'easy2edit: trees and contributions' on the Super admin overview, showing a growing tree, tiles, charts and costs. This requires an Ecologi link in Admin > API keys (Impact API key, with an optional username for public figures).

Four sources contribute trees:

- Website visitors, one tree per N page views.
- Machine and energy use, offsetting estimated CO2.
- Use of easy2edit by the user, a fixed number of trees per month.
- Trees planted by easy2edit itself.

A monthly maximum limits automatic settlement, and test mode is on by default, so nothing is actually purchased until switched off. Trees are named after the website or after easy2edit.

At site level, Admin > System > Trees and gifts (module 'ecologi_admin') lets an administrator set a monthly contribution, choose per function, visitors, new users, AI use, energy use, a 'one tree per N' rate, set a maximum per month, and give trees immediately. Its tabs are My contribution, Costs and result, and History.

On the easy2edit server, the Site manager shows a Trees tab per website (status, trees, expected costs per part, costs per month, switches and monthly maximum), and an overview 'Plant trees: all websites' reachable from the Site manager page, listing figures per company and per website with totals. The Site manager also has a Websites tab to update websites or force an update.

On the public website, next to 'powered by (c) easy2edit <year>', a leaf icon opens an energy window with two tabs: 'Plant trees' (showing a tree filling toward its next milestone, the donated amount, this month's figures, sources, a chart and a 'More info' link to https://easy2edit.com/#groen) and 'Energy'.

The installation wizard includes a step 'Plant trees'; the Ecologi link to easy2edit is always on.

## Cache and energy advice

The cache can be shared across the system, using the database by default, or Redis or memory, configured in Admin > System, alongside a system cache for speed and related energy advice.

Admin > Cache lets you choose where the cache is kept (database, memory or Redis), set how many seconds the system cache lasts (5 minutes by default), and restart the cache with a button. Redis is installed by the deployment script as a service and is used by default when it responds; if Redis is unavailable, the system falls back to the database.

Admin > Energy shows the website's energy label, energy advice in two columns with a switch per piece of advice, a run window with progress, cache advice, and AI prompt buttons for every open point. The energy label can also be shown on the website itself.

## API keys and reseller defaults

In Admin > API keys, a super admin has an Update button that checks keys against the easy2edit server and updates them when needed. This requires either a code sent by e-mail or SMS, or an account on easy2edit.com, the master server. During installation, keys travel encrypted inside an installation file locked with a password, and are unpacked and installed at the destination.

The default reseller tab always requires phone numbers with a country code, and the default settings tabs include a 'do not overwrite' option per tab, both standard parts of the settings.

## Website design

Admin > Website > Design is always present in the menu and as a tile. If a part of it is not installed or switched on, easy2edit prompts you to install and switch it on, showing the cost and the steps with progress. This section cannot be switched off.

## Light and dark mode

Screenshots, videos and help content in easy2edit exist in both light and dark mode. The HTML manual and Help show whichever mode the reader is using, while the PDF manual is always shown in light mode.
